title: Completed extension-by-zero base change
statement:
Let $(A,I)$ satisfy [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], and let
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
U'&\xrightarrow{g_U}&U\\
j'\downarrow&&\downarrow j\\
X'&\xrightarrow{g}&X
\end{array}
$$
be a cartesian open-immersion square [def-cbc-open-immersion-square]. Assume in addition that $j$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Use the completed coefficient sheaves $A_T=\varprojlim_n(A/I^n)_T$ and $D(T_{\Proet},A)=D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_T))$ of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Identify $A_X|_U=A_U$ and $A_{X'}|_{U'}=A_{U'}$ under the slice-site identifications [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. Extension by zero $j_!$ and $j'_!$ means sheafification of the extension-by-zero module presheaf on these ringed slice sites [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf, def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], applied termwise to complexes. Let $K\in D(U_{\Proet},A)$ be derived $I$-complete [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion]. Then $j_!K$ is derived $I$-complete, and the canonical completed base-change map
$$
Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}j_!K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }j'_!Lg_{U,\mathrm{comp}}^*K
$$
is an isomorphism, natural in $K$, where completed pullback is [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. Both sides belong to the derived $I$-complete subcategory of $D(X'_{\Proet},A)$. The canonical map is the one induced by the finite-coefficient extension-by-zero base-change maps and the comparison between extension by zero and the derived limit of the strict reduction tower.

proof.text: For $T=X,X',U,U'$ put $P_n=A/I^n$ and use the completed sheaf $A_T$ of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. For each pair $(T,W)=(X,U),(X',U')$, [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] identifies $W$'s pro-etale site with the slice site and carries each constant $(P_n)_T$ to $(P_n)_W$. The sectionwise formula for limits [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-limits-sectionwise] therefore identifies $A_T|_W$ with $A_W$: on an object $V\to W$ both are the compatible families of sections of $(P_n)_T(V)$. The componentwise identity preserves every projection and quotient map. Since the square is cartesian and $j$ is quasi-compact, [lem-pc-quasi-compact-base-change] makes $j'$ quasi-compact too; there is no quasi-compactness requirement on $g$.

source.place: Tag 09AE (definition-extension-zero), slice interpretation; schemes.tex Tag 01K5 (quasi-compact base change).

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] to these ringed slice sites. Restriction and sheafified extension by zero are exact, and extension is left adjoint to restriction. Thus [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] supplies their termwise functors on unbounded derived categories. We will also use extension with coefficients $(P_n)_T$; it is the same finite-coefficient functor as [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero]. Extension commutes with restriction of scalars along $A_T\to(P_n)_T$ and along $P_b\to P_a$. Indeed [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf] uses the same direct-sum presheaf of abelian groups before and after scalar restriction, with action composed with the ring map [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]; [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] equips the same abelian sheafification with the unique extending action. The resulting comparison is identity on the underlying abelian sheaf and is natural in every module map. No completed coefficient sheaf is identified with the constant sheaf $A$.

Let $e:W\hookrightarrow T$ be either $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ or $j':U'\hookrightarrow X'$, and let $C$ be any complex on $W$. Choose a K-flat representative $P\to C$ with flat terms by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The module tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-extension-tensor] extends to total tensor complexes: $e_!$ commutes with the direct sums in the totalization because it is a left adjoint [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits], and the comparison commutes with the differentials in [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. For any acyclic $A_T$-complex $N$, restriction $e^*N$ is acyclic by Step 2, so
$$ (e_!P)\otimes_{A_T}N\cong e_!(P\otimes_{A_W}e^*N) $$
is acyclic. Thus $e_!P$ is K-flat by [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Its terms are flat too: for each $q$ the same tensor comparison expresses $(-)\otimes e_!P^q$ as restriction, tensor with the flat $P^q$, and exact extension, which is exact [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Since extension is exact, $e_!P\to e_!C$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The reduction of $e_!C$ is consequently computed by $(e_!P)\otimes_{A_T}(P_n)_T$, and the tensor comparison identifies this with $e_!(P\otimes_{A_W}(P_n)_W)$. By [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] these identify the strict reduction towers
$$ (e_!C)_\bullet\cong e_!(C_\bullet). $$
At the presheaf tensor level the comparison sends a generator $s\otimes u$ in the unique summand indexed by a factorization $V\to W$ to the same tensor $s\otimes u$. Applying $q_{b,a}$ on either side sends it to $s\otimes q_{b,a}(u)$, so the comparisons commute with the actual tower maps, not just with their evaluations. Step 2 supplies the scalar-restriction identification on each level. The construction is natural on K-flat representatives and hence in $C$.

source.place: Tag 0E8I (lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor); sites-cohomology.tex Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution) and 06YN (definition-K-flat). The extension to total complexes and quotient maps is written out here.

proof.text:
Here is the product argument needed in the imported proof (Stacks Tag 09BP), using existing nodes rather than introducing a product lemma. Let $e:W\hookrightarrow T$ be either $j$ or $j'$, let $R=A_T$, and let $(F_s)_{s\in S}$ be a small family of $R|_W$-module sheaves. Choose a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ with image $T\setminus W$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-closed-subscheme]. For any $R|_W$-module sheaf $F$, put $H=e_*F$. One has $e^{-1}H=F$: on $V\to W$ the direct-image formula [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] evaluates $H$ as $F(V\times_TW)=F(V)$, under the slice identification of [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. Since $e$ is quasi-compact, the exact sequence of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed], applied to $H$, identifies
$$ e_!F=\ker\big(e_*F\longrightarrow i_*i^{-1}e_*F\big). $$
Both direct images preserve products by the same sectionwise direct-image formula and [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-limits-sectionwise]. Closed inverse image $i^{-1}$ preserves small limits, including products, by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-immersion-limit-preservation], with target coefficient $i^{-1}R$ (no unrelated scalar extension). Therefore the kernel for $F=\prod_sF_s$ is the product of the kernels for $F_s$: on each section both consist of tuples whose every component maps to zero. Under these identifications the map is precisely the comparison induced by the projections. Hence $e_!(\prod_sF_s)\to\prod_se_!F_s$ is an isomorphism, natural in the family. This is a kernel computation from the cited statements, not an assertion that extension is sectionwise zero on arbitrary test schemes. It includes the empty family.

source.place: Tag 09BP (lemma-j-shriek-limits), kernel proof, using Tag 09AA (lemma-closed-immersion). The stated ringed recollement and module limit nodes supply its module version.

proof.text: Countable products in $\operatorname{Mod}(A_T)$ and $\operatorname{Mod}(A_W)$ are exact by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact]. Thus [lem-weil-derived-limit-products-core] identifies their derived products with termwise product complexes. Step 4 applied in every cochain degree gives preservation of these products by $e_!$. For a family of strict towers $M_{s,\bullet}$, their product has level $n$ equal to $\prod_sM_{s,n}$ and transition characterized by its projections as the $s$-th transition after projection. The product universal property at each level proves this is a product of towers. Exactness is levelwise by [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian], so their countable products are exact too. Termwise extension commutes with evaluation and preserves these products, and is exact by Step 2. This verifies the hypotheses for the canonical strict-limit comparison in the next step.

source.place: Returned Step 5, first paragraph: exact product and strict-tower hypotheses.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit] to the module functor $F=e_!$ for either $(W,T)=(U,X)$ or $(U',X')$, with exactness from Step 2 and product preservation from Steps 4-5. It supplies a natural isomorphism
$$\lambda_e:e_!R\lim M_\bullet\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim(e_!M_\bullet).$$
Use its specified signed Roos model, not an arbitrary cone comparison: $H(M)^q=P(M)^q\oplus P(M)^{q-1}$, $d(x,y)=(dx,(1-s)x-dy)$, and $\lambda_e=\theta_{e_!M}^{-1}\kappa_Me_!(\theta_M)$. Here $\kappa$ is the canonical product comparison on both summands. The cited statement identifies this with the resolution/ordinary-limit comparison, gives both Roos-triangle equations, and preserves maps induced by strict augmentations. These are exactly the canonicality and unit properties required below.

source.place: Returned Step 5, functorial Roos construction, canonical resolution comparison, and two structure-map equations.

proof.text: Extension by zero also preserves intrinsic derived completeness. In [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion], the Koszul complex $Q_m(A_T)$ is a bounded finite free complex. Its restriction is $Q_m(A_W)$ with the same differential multiplications $a_j^m$ and transition multiplications $a_j$. The tensor comparison of Step 3, or its finite-sum version, identifies $e_!(C\otimes Q_m(A_W))$ with $(e_!C)\otimes Q_m(A_T)$. Step 4 identifies their termwise countable products. Since $e_!$ is additive, it identifies the operator $(z_m)\mapsto(z_m-t_mz_{m+1})$ and the two finite summands and differential of the explicitly defined completion fiber $F(C)$. Moreover, both completion units send $c$ to $((c\otimes1)_m,0)$, so $e_!\eta_C$ is identified with $\eta_{e_!C}$. Consequently $C$ complete implies $e_!C$ complete. Apply this first to $j$ and the given $K$, making $Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}j_!K$ well-typed. By [lemma-weil-pbc-completed-pullback-reduction], $L=Lg_{U,\mathrm{comp}}^*K$ is complete; apply the same argument to $j'$ and $L$. That lemma applied to $g$ and $j_!K$ also gives completeness of the left-hand side. Thus the displayed comparison will be a map between complete objects.

source.place: Tag 09BP combined with the Koszul completion model; algebraization.tex Tag 0A0E (lemma-derived-completion-koszul). The chain-level units are the specified units of the cited intrinsic definition.

proof.text:
For each $P_n=A/I^n$, finiteness is part of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], and [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact] identifies finite module pullback with exact inverse image. Apply [lem-cbc-finite-open-exchange-scalars] to $P_b\to P_a$ for all $b\ge a\ge1$. The canonical finite exchanges
$$\beta_n:g_n^*j_!K_n\xrightarrow{\sim}j'_!g_{U,n}^*K_n$$
and their inverse adjoint mates commute with every strict quotient transition and are natural in chain maps. Combined with the strict reduction comparison of Step 3, they give inverse maps of strict towers. The natural finite-reduction isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] identify the actual completed-coefficient derived pullback towers of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] with these finite models, including their transition maps. Thus this is a tower isomorphism for the specified derived pullback, not merely a family of isomorphisms after evaluation.

source.place: Returned Step 7, finite exchange, coefficient restrictions and strict reduction-tower comparison.

proof.text: When changing the presentation of the specified pullback, apply [lem-cbc-adic-pullback-presentation-transport] to $g$ and to $g_U$. The coefficient structure maps are the maps of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]: their $n$-th components are the canonical constant-section maps after the finite projections. Hence the hypotheses on the components hold, and the cited lemma identifies the coefficient maps and the natural module pullbacks. Its universal counit equations then give the ordinary and actual strict-tower derived comparisons, respecting every quotient transition. This retains the inverse-adjoint-mate normalization of Step 8 in any of these presentations and imposes no invertibility hypothesis on the completed coefficient map.

source.place: Returned Step 7, coefficient projections, universal derived-pair counits and change of presentation.

proof.text:
Apply the functorial derived inverse limit [prop-weil-pbc-rlim-functoriality] to the strict tower isomorphism of Step 8. By [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] and the reduction comparison of Step 3, its source is $Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}j_!K$ and target is $R\lim_n(j'_!g_{U,n}^*K_n)$. Follow it by $\lambda_{j'}^{-1}$ of Step 6:
$$Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}j_!K\xrightarrow{R\lim\beta}R\lim_n(j'_!g_{U,n}^*K_n)\xrightarrow{\lambda_{j'}^{-1}}j'_!R\lim_n(g_{U,n}^*K_n)=j'_!Lg^*_{U,\mathrm{comp}}K.$$
Both arrows are isomorphisms. Their constituents are natural in $K$, so the composite is natural. It is the canonical map of the statement, induced by the finite exchanges and the specified strict-limit comparison. Step 7 establishes completeness of $j_!K$ before completed pullback is applied, and completeness of both resulting endpoints.

source.place: Returned Step 8, first paragraph: derived-limit assembly of the completed exchange.

proof.text: For the presentation transports of Step 9, [lem-cbc-adic-pullback-presentation-transport] gives $E_gu_g=u'_ge_g$ and the same identity for $g_U$, where $u_g,u'_g$ are the specified ordinary-to-completed units and $e_g$ is the counit-normalized ordinary comparison. These are the units of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. The strict quotient augmentation is $x\mapsto x\otimes1$ at every level. By [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit], $\lambda_{j'}$ preserves the maps induced by these strict augmentations; in the signed fiber coordinates their value is $(x,0)$. Thus transporting Step 10 by $E_g^{-1}$ on the source and $j'_!E_{g_U}$ on the target preserves the finite inverse-adjoint-mate normalization. This is the original normalization assertion, now supplied by cited lemmas on the actual tower functors and their counits.

source.place: Returned Step 8, second paragraph: completion units, strict augmentations and presentation-independent normalization.

proof_origin.place: Retained finite-reduction/strict-derived-limit route; returned Steps 5 and 7 extracted into three statement-only tool lemmas and the existing normalized strict Roos model. Eleven proof steps.

split_report.summary: STATEMENT-DISPUTED: the imported arbitrary-open statement can be ill-typed because non-quasi-compact extension by zero need not preserve derived completeness. Added quasi-compactness of j, explicitly retained completed coefficient categories, and proved completeness plus the canonical natural comparison in eight steps. No new nodes: Stacks 09BP product preservation is a kernel step using the existing ringed recollement and closed-immersion limit theorems. Audited finite-coefficient transition compatibility and supplied exact statement quotes for every citation. Mathlib searches and their unavailable results are recorded from searches.jsonl. Second reading supplied the levelwise countable-product construction for towers and made the two-open arguments uniform. Repair of landing return: revalidated current cited statements, replaced the obsolete canonical-map use of lem-cbc-exact-functor-rlim by an explicit functorial resolution comparison with both Roos equations, and refreshed stale quotes for the finite exchange and Rlim functoriality. Current second reading repaired the remaining unstated fiber-model identification in Step 5 using the existing general K-injective tower Roos-complex comparison and an explicit natural zigzag. NY second reading (stage 1): restored the missing verbatim citation file; checked all eight steps against the current cited statements and local sources; made the Step 4 module binder explicit and wrote the chain homotopy used to descend the Step 5 fiber functor. Refreshed proof_origin to the current blueprint and removed its obsolete missing-source assertion. No new nodes or Mathlib leaves; the retained stage-2 material is historical and is not packaged by deliver.py. Current NY repair re-read the maintenance return and archived binding, removed the stale sandbox lean field to match the current base, and explicitly specified finite coefficient projection equations, derived-pair counit normalization and constant-tower quotient-unit compatibility in Steps 7-8. The new citation is the existing resolving-class universal-pair theorem. Stage 2 remains deferred: no Lean was written or compiled, no reviewed binding is claimed, and the old public API is not changed. NN repair of the human re-split return: unchanged statement and Lean record; original Steps 1-4 and 6 retained verbatim. Extracted canonical exact-product-functor Rlim comparison, coefficient-compatible finite open exchange, and counit/quotient-unit-compatible adic presentation transport as three unsplit nodes. Reused the existing normalized strict Roos comparison as the fiber model. All non-elementary steps now have at most 2000 characters; final assembly and normalization are separated without changing their route. Previous NY report preserved in the sandbox scratchpad.
split_report.blueprint: Original exactness/reduction-tower sentences: Steps 1-3. Corrected quasi-compact product parenthetical: Steps 4-5. Canonical strict-limit comparison: Step 6 and lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit (using existing lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison). Intrinsic completeness: Step 7 (returned Step 6 unchanged). Finite exchange and quotient compatibility: Step 8 and lem-cbc-finite-open-exchange-scalars. Coefficient/presentation/counit normalization: Step 9 and lem-cbc-adic-pullback-presentation-transport. Derived-limit assembly and quotient-unit compatibility: Steps 10-11.

tool_uses.why: Identifies open pro-etale sites with ringed slice sites and restricts constant coefficients; the finite-coefficient nodes of this unit do not provide the completed coefficient identification.
Computes module limits and coefficient inverse limits sectionwise; needed for completed sheaves and the product-kernel calculation.
Supplies exact extension/restriction on any ringed slice site, including the nonfinite completed coefficient ring sheaf; the unit finite-coefficient statement does not cover this.
Passes the exact module functors termwise to unbounded derived categories.
Provides a K-flat representative with flat terms for the reduction-tower computation.
General module tensor comparison for extension by zero; used to prove K-flatness and reduction compatibility directly.
Gives the ringed short exact recollement sequence needed for the kernel proof of product preservation, with quasi-compact open hypothesis explicitly verified.
Supplies all-limit preservation for closed inverse image in the product-kernel argument; the target unit has no such geometric lemma.
Exact countable products of arbitrary ring-sheaf modules on the pro-etale site.
Identifies termwise products with products in unbounded derived categories under exactness.
Proves completed pullback is complete, needed for both sides and the application to j_!K after Step 6.
Identifies finite module pullback with exact inverse image; does not assume the completed ring structure map is an isomorphism.
